nodes.label: Burst pipe causing sudden flooding
nodes.action_plan: DO: Locate and turn off the main stopcock/shut-off valve immediately. Isolate nearby electrics if safe. DO NOT: Attempt to bind the pipe with tape while under pressure or use unapproved temporary fittings.

nodes.label: Toilet overflowing continuously
nodes.action_plan: DO: Turn off the toilet water supply valve located behind or near the base of the toilet. Clean contaminated areas safely. DO NOT: Keep flushing in an attempt to clear it.

nodes.label: Water heater leaking heavily
nodes.action_plan: DO: Turn off the cold water supply to the heater and shut off its power source (gas or electric). DO NOT: Touch the hot water tank or attempt to plug the pressure relief valve.

nodes.label: Burning smell coming from a plug socket
nodes.action_plan: DO: Turn off the circuit breaker immediately at the main panel. Unplug devices only if safe to do so without touching the socket face. DO NOT: Ignore the smell or use the socket.

nodes.label: Live wires exposed or burning smell from sockets
nodes.action_plan: DO: Isolate power at the main consumer unit/breaker panel immediately using safe isolation procedures. DO NOT: Touch the wires even if power appears off; do not attempt DIY repairs on live circuits.

nodes.label: RCD or GFCI continuously tripping
nodes.action_plan: DO: Unplug all appliances on the affected circuit and attempt to reset. If it trips again, leave it off and call a professional. DO NOT: Tape the breaker switch up or bypass the safety switch.

nodes.label: Gas leak or strong smell of gas
nodes.action_plan: DO: Open all windows/doors immediately; turn off the emergency control valve at the meter; vacate the premises. DO NOT: Use electrical switches, smoke, or use mobile phones inside. Safety note: Incomplete combustion (yellow flame) indicates deadly Carbon Monoxide.

nodes.label: Gas Safe Register / UK Gas Safety Regs
Carbon monoxide alarm sounding
nodes.action_plan: DO: Evacuate the property immediately, leave doors open to ventilate, and call emergency services or the gas emergency number. DO NOT: Stay inside to try and find the source.

nodes.label: Yellow or orange flame on gas boiler or hob
nodes.action_plan: DO: Stop using the appliance immediately, turn off the gas supply, and ventilate the room. DO NOT: Ignore it; a yellow flame indicates incomplete combustion and deadly carbon monoxide.

nodes.label: Institution of Gas Engineers and Managers (IGEM)
Key snapped off inside the lock cylinder
nodes.action_plan: DO: Leave the broken piece inside and call a professional for extraction. DO NOT: Try to dig it out with pins or screwdrivers as this pushes it further in and destroys the pins.

nodes.label: Broken lock or burglary repair (uPVC/Timber doors)
nodes.action_plan: DO: Secure the property immediately. For timber doors, ensure BS 3621 certified locks are used. For uPVC doors, upgrade to SS 312 Diamond cylinders to prevent lock snapping. DO NOT: Compromise fire escape routes by adding non-compliant locks.

nodes.label: Sewage backing up into shower or ground floor fixtures
nodes.action_plan: DO: Stop using all water in the house immediately to prevent further flooding. DO NOT: Pour harsh chemical unblockers down the drain as they will sit in the pipe and endanger the engineer.

nodes.label: Sinkhole appearing near exterior drain pipe
nodes.action_plan: DO: Keep people and vehicles completely away from the area; call a drainage specialist for a CCTV survey. DO NOT: Walk near the edge or attempt to fill it with dirt without fixing the collapsed pipe.

nodes.label: Shattered sliding glass door or low-level window
nodes.action_plan: DO: Keep pets and children out of the room; apply heavy-duty tape over cracks if the pane is still intact. DO NOT: Try to remove large, jagged shards without heavy protective gloves and eyewear.

nodes.label: Condensation permanently trapped between double glazed panes
nodes.action_plan: DO: Arrange for the sealed glass unit to be measured and replaced by a professional. DO NOT: Attempt to drill holes in the glass to let the moisture out; this destroys the thermal efficiency completely.

nodes.label: Water pouring through ceiling during heavy storm
nodes.action_plan: DO: Place buckets to catch water; safely pierce a small hole in a bulging plaster ceiling to release trapped water. DO NOT: Climb onto a wet, slippery roof during a storm to attempt temporary repairs.

nodes.label: Roofline visibly sagging from the outside
nodes.action_plan: DO: Evacuate the area directly below the sag and request a structural roofing inspection immediately. DO NOT: Attempt to prop it up from the inside without structural calculations.

nodes.label: Large, stepped cracks appearing in exterior brickwork
nodes.action_plan: DO: Monitor the crack with a gauge; check for internal symptoms like sticking doors or sloping floors. DO NOT: Simply fill the crack with mortar without having a structural engineer identify the root cause.

nodes.label: Removing an internal timber stud wall or plasterboard partition
nodes.action_plan: DO: Hire a structural engineer to survey the wall before any demolition. Timber stud walls often support upper floor joists or roof loads. DO NOT: Assume a timber wall is non-load-bearing just because it is not brick; removing a structural timber wall can cause ceiling collapse or structural sagging.

nodes.label: Flooded basement with standing water
nodes.action_plan: DO: Turn off the electricity to the basement from the main breaker panel located upstairs or outside. DO NOT: Wade into floodwater if the power is still on or if it smells of raw sewage.

nodes.label: Extensive black mould covering walls or ceiling
nodes.action_plan: DO: Wear an N95 mask if in the room; improve ventilation; identify and fix the underlying moisture leak. DO NOT: Dry-brush the mould or scrape it, as this releases millions of toxic spores into the air.

nodes.label: Vehicle loses power entirely on a busy highway
nodes.action_plan: DO: Indicate and pull over to the hard shoulder; turn on hazard lights immediately; exit from the non-traffic side. DO NOT: Stay inside the vehicle if parked in a live lane, and do not stand directly behind the vehicle.

nodes.label: Engine temperature gauge hits the red zone/smoking
nodes.action_plan: DO: Pull over safely and turn the engine off immediately to prevent catastrophic block warping. DO NOT: Open the radiator cap while the engine is hot, as boiling coolant will spray out under high pressure.

nodes.label: AC unit blowing warm air and making a hissing sound
nodes.action_plan: DO: Turn the system off at the thermostat to prevent burning out the compressor motor. DO NOT: Attempt to top up the refrigerant yourself; venting fluorinated gases into the atmosphere is illegal.

nodes.label: Furnace smells strongly like burning dust or electrical burning
nodes.action_plan: DO: If it's the first time turning it on for winter, let it run for 10 minutes to burn off dust. If the smell persists or smells like melting plastic, turn it off immediately. DO NOT: Store flammable materials near the unit.
